messages:
mohamed: seeing a weird spike in ECC/Xid errors in us-west2 starting ~09:12 UTC, capacity dropped ~11% because we auto-drained a bunch of nodes. logs show NIC egress flaps around the same time. filing here to correlate :thinking_face:

jensen: can you paste the node list and a few error lines? I saw some telemetry lag alerts earlier but assumed noisy probes. :eyes:

mohamed: node ids: gpu-usw2-rack21-{12,13,14,15,16,17,18}. sample kernel lines: `GPU0 Xid 79` and repeated `CE ECC corrected` bursts. also seeing repeated `NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0: transmit queue 0 timed out` on the same hosts.

claire: ops-bot shows bulk drain triggered by automated healthpolicy at 09:16UTC after 3 consecutive Xid events. are the drains due to on-node NV driver crashes or network-induced telemetry gaps?

ops-bot: Alert: `telemetry-lag-high` triggered for cluster-us-west2 at 09:14UTC. Auto-drain policy executed against 7 hosts.

jensen: my hunch: if egress NIC flaps cause our telemetry agent to fail to flush KV caches, the runtime may mis-evaluate GPU liveness and escalate. we saw similar pattern in a small canary last month but not this scale.

luis: agreed. I pulled interface stats: `ifconfig eth0` shows Tx errors and `dmesg` has multiple `mlx5_core` reset messages. looks like a switch flap causing packet storms.

mohamed: reproducing tail of journal on one host: ```
Mar 12 09:13:42 gpu-usw2-rack21-15 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: Firmware error, resetting device
Mar 12 09:13:42 gpu-usw2-rack21-15 kernel: NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0: transmit queue 0 timed out
Mar 12 09:13:43 gpu-usw2-rack21-15 runtime: kv-cache-sync failed: timeout
Mar 12 09:13:44 gpu-usw2-rack21-15 runtime: gpu-health: Xid 79 detected on GPU0
```

claire: ok. immediate actions: 1) pause auto-drain policy for the affected host set (prevent churn while we root cause) 2) cordon and manual probe only targeted hosts 3) escalate to networking to check switch logs and fabric.

lara: (added offline) networking team: we see a flapping port on leaf-42 at 09:12UTC, likely correlates. working on clearing error counters and mapping physical port.

jensen: to pause drains: `curl -XPOST "$CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/health/policies/pause" -d '{"selector":"gpu-usw2-rack21"}'` — do we have permission?

mohamed: I can run that. doing now.

mohamed: done — pauses in place. also re-enabled verbose telemetry upload to S3 for the window 09:05-09:25 for offline analysis.

luis: I'm running `ethtool -S eth0` across affected nodes to collect stats and saving to /tmp/netstats-usw2-flap.tar.gz. pushing to /mnt/shared for ops.

claire: next: decide whether to un-drain nodes once fabric cleared. propose: manual health check (memtest quick, smi query, short perf run) and if green, bring back with gradual ramp to avoid burst KV/telemetry.

tara: cost/impact note: we lost ~11% capacity for ~40 minutes = ~120 GPU-hours lost on peak. if we bring all nodes back at once we risk another telemetry surge and further auto-drains. recommend staged 2-node batches per minute.

jensen: also flagging to runtime team: consider adding transient-telemetry-suppression rule when packet loss > 5% for a host to prevent misclassifying Xid bursts caused by upstream drops.

mohamed: networking confirmed leaf-42 port module hardware fault. replacement ETA 2h. will keep paused drains until they swap hardware and we validate.

claire: thanks. action items assigned: networking to replace module (networking), infra to validate nodes post-repair (mohamed/jensen/luis), runtime to evaluate suppression rule (eng-runtime backlog ticket), ops to update incident doc with GPU-hours impact (tara).

ops-bot: Incident note created: `INC-2024-03-gpu-net-flap-usw2` — severity P2 — participants paged.

mohamed: updating oncall log and will post postmortem summary once we've validated recovery. :thumbsup:
